gloss: self-important; stuck-up; acting like a big shot

definitions.gloss: self-important; stuck-up; acting like a big shot
definitions.explanation: Describes someone who behaves as if they were more important or knowledgeable than they are. Always critical — it describes the impression the person gives, not their actual standing.

examples.japanese: {偉|えら}そうな{顔|かお}をしている。
examples.english: He has a self-important look on his face.

examples.japanese: {新人|しんじん}なのに{偉|えら}そうに{指示|しじ}を{出|だ}す。
examples.english: He's new here, yet he gives orders like he's in charge.

examples.japanese: {偉|えら}そうなことを{言|い}ってしまったが、{自分|じぶん}もまだできていないと{気|き}づいた。
examples.english: I said something high-handed, but then realized I can't do it myself yet either.

notes:
{偉|えら}い (great, admirable) plus the suffix そう (seeming). Because そう describes appearance rather than fact, {偉|えら}そう means "acting great" — and in practice always implies the person is not.

USAGE:
Behaves as a na-adjective: {偉|えら}そうな{態度|たいど} (a self-important attitude), {偉|えら}そうに{話|はな}す (to talk like a big shot). The adverbial {偉|えら}そうに is the most common form.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {偉|えら}そうな{態度|たいど}: an arrogant manner
- {偉|えら}そうに{言|い}う: to say something in a high-handed way
- {偉|えら}そうにするな: don't act so important

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {生意気|なまいき}: cheeky, impudent — stronger, and typically aimed at someone younger or junior
- {威張|いば}る: to throw one's weight around — a verb describing the behavior itself
